Regular list
 High C0Urt 0F Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Srinagar
 Owp 1567/2015
 Mst. Rehmat Begum ...Petitioner(s)/Appellant(s)
 Through: Mr. Bilal Ahmad Malla, Adv.
 Vs.
 State of Jk & Ors.

...Respondent(s)
 Through: Mr. Ilias Laway, Ga.
 Mr. Syed Musaib, Dy. Ag.
 Coram:Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Sekhri, Judge
 Judgment
1. Petitioner claims to be recorded owner of a double storied residential house, including a shop and land appurtenant thereto, measuring 04 Sarsai situate at Reshipora Cherat, Tehsil Kakapora.

Case of the petitioner is that aforesaid residential house came under the alignment of newly constructed road Banderpora Cherat to Reshipora Cherat Package and respondent no. 4-Executive Engineer,
PMGSY, Division Pulwama, made assessment of the aforesaid structure and her case was forwarded to the higher authorities for compensation in lieu of acquisition.

2. Allegation of the petitioner is that since her house fell within the zone of Reshipora, she surrendered possession of the said house to PMGSY and her house came to be demolished by the respondents.

3. The grievance of the petitioner is that when she approached the respondents no. 1 & 2, for compensation, she received a communication dated 27.01.2015, i.e., after a gap of three years and after her house was demolished by the respondents that her land has not been utilized for the construction of the road in question.

4. Petitioner has invoked writ jurisdiction of this Court, for issuance of appropriate writs, primarily on the ground that she cannot be deprived of her property otherwise than in due course of law and Mst. Rehmat Begum vs State Of Jk & Ors on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124572862/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: consequent mandamus to the respondents to pay compensation for the structure alleged to have been demolished by them for the construction of road from Banderpora Cherat to Reshipora Cherat District Pulwama.

5. Per contra, respondents, at the outset have questioned maintainability of the present petition on the ground that petitioner has raised disputed questions of fact, which cannot gone into by this Court in exercise of writ jurisdiction.

6. Countervailing the factual stand of the petitioner, respondent no. 4 in the counter affidavit is affront with the contention that the indenting Department constructed the road in question i.e.,
Banderpora Cherat to Reshipora Cherat under Package No. JK10-85 in the year 2012.
Initially, the proposed length of the road in DPR was 2000 metres, however, during the actual execution the habitation got connected within 1750 metres.
The assessment case was framed for full length but notices for execution under Section (4) were issued only to those land owners whose structure was falling within the constructed length.
It is stand of the respondents that mere framing of assessment does not mean that petitioner is entitled for compensation.
7. It is also contention of the respondents that since the land/structure of the petitioner was not required, therefore, there was no question of surrender certificate.

The respondent no. 4, in the counter affidavit has disputed the surrender certificate produced by the petitioner as fake and same has been communicated to Collector Land Acquisition by respondent no. 4-Executive Engineer, vide his communication No. EE/PMGSY/P/2538-39 dated 08.01.2013.

Respondents have annexed Geo-tagged photographs of the disputed structure to demonstrate that the structure in question is intact on the spot and has not been acquired or demolished by the indenting Department.

8. Having heard rival contentions of the parties, I have gone through the record produced by Mr.
Ilias Laway, learned Government Advocate appearing for the respondents.

9. While, it is trite and well recognized that right to hold property is a basic human right akin to a fundamental right guaranteed in terms of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India and nobody can be deprived of his/her right to property, otherwise than in due course of law.

However, it is equally well settled that disputed questions of fact cannot be gone into and adjudicated by the High Court,
in exercise of writ jurisdiction.

10. Hon'ble Supreme Court in "State of Rajasthan vs. Bhawani Singh & Ors."; 1993 Supp(1) SCC 306, in a similar fact situation has held that disputed question relating to title cannot be satisfactorily gone into in a writ petition.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan vs. Bhawani Singh & Ors."; 1993 Supp(1) SCC 306
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant extract of the judgment reads as below:-
"Having heard the counsel for the parties, we are of the opinion, that the writ petition was misconceived insofar as it asked for, in effect, a declaration of writ petitioner's title to the said plot.
It is evident from the facts stated hereinabove that the title of the writ petitioner is very much in dispute.

Disputed question relating to title cannot be satisfactorily gone into or adjudicated in a writ petition."

sentences.text: 11. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. Karan Singh vs. State of J&K & Anr.; (2004) 5 SCC 698 has made identical observation with respect to jurisdiction of the writ court in relation to disputed questions of fact.

entities.text: Dr. Karan Singh vs. State of J&K & Anr.; (2004) 5 SCC 698
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant extract of the judgment reads as below:-
"As already noticed, there has never been any declaration that the articles in question are private properties of the appellant or his father.
The correspondence between Maharaja Hari Singh and the Government does not declare these articles as private property of the Maharaja though some other properties were so declared.

Assuming there is some substance in the claim of the appellant which requires consideration,
then it will depend upon examination of various disputed questions of facts.
Such disputed questions cannot be adjudicated except on taking of evidence.

In Dharam Dutt v. Union of India a case of taking over of Sapru House by promulgation of ordinance followed by the Act, the contention of the writ petitioners was that the building, the library and all other movables in Sapru House are owned by the Society and takeover by the Government has deprived the Society of its property without any authority of law.

entities.text: Dharam Dutt v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court noticing that the Union of India do not admit title of the petitioner and also noticing that there is not one document of title produced by the petitioners, held that such highly disputed questions of fact which cannot be determined except on evidence are not fit to be taken up for adjudication in the exercise of writ jurisdiction."
(Underlining by me)
12.

Similar observations have been made by Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Union of India (UOI) and Ors. Vs. Puna Hinda"; AIR 2021 SC 4187 and "Orissa Agro Industries Corporation Ltd. & Ors vs.
Bharati Industries and Ors"; AIR 2006 SC 198.
13.

entities.text: Union of India (UOI) and Ors. Vs. Puna Hinda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Orissa Agro Industries Corporation Ltd. & Ors vs.
Bharati Industries and Ors"; AIR 2006 SC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is evident from the aforequoted observations made by the Apex Court that there may be cases where High Court in exercise of its writ jurisdiction may decide rival claims by referring to the contentions raised in the affidavits and counter-affidavits and perusal of the official record,
however, seriously disputed questions of facts or rival claims of the parties, those are required to be investigated and determined purely on the basis of evidence to be led by the parties cannot be gone into and adjudicated upon in exercise of its writ jurisdiction.
14.

As already discussed above, allegations of the petitioner that her double storied residential house was not only acquired and dismantled by the respondents but assessment of compensation was also made have been seriously disputed by respondent no. 4 in the counter affidavit by stating that,
structure of the petitioner in question was neither acquired nor dismantled by the indenting Department.

Respondent no. 4, admitted that initially proposed length of the road in question in the DPR was 2000 metres, but since during the actual execution, the habitation got connected within 1750 metres and the exercise to go further for 2000 metres involved huge expenditure and was not covered in the DPR, therefore, structure in question was never acquired by the respondents.

The certificate with respect to surrender of possession of the disputed structure by the petitioner annexed with the petition has been seriously disputed by the respondents as fake and perusal of the Mst. Rehmat Begum vs State Of Jk & Ors on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124572862/
3

entities.text: Mst. Rehmat Begum vs State Of Jk & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: record reveals that respondent no. 4, has even communicated to Collector Land Acquisition (Assistant Commissioner, Revenue) Pulwama, for verification of the said certificate, on the premise that same was never issued by him.

15. It is clear from the pleadings of the parties that there are serious allegations and counter allegations and rival claims, which are required to be investigated and can be determined by a competent civil Court only after proper trial and evidence.
Mere valuation of property or assessment would not confer any right to land owner to ask for compensation.
Such disputed facts cannot be gone into and adjudicated by this court exercising prerogative of issuing writs.
16. Since the acquisition as also alleged demolition has been disputed by the respondents, the disputed facts cannot be gone into by this Court in exercise of writ jurisdiction.
17. Having regard to the aforesaid, present petition being devoid of merit is dismissed with connected CM(s).
However, petitioner shall be at liberty to avail appropriate remedy as per law.
18. Interim direction, if any, shall stand vacated.

; 
(RAJESH SEKHRI) JUDGE SRINAGAR 14.03.2024
Hilal Ahmad
